subject: mathematics
question_text: If 0 < x < π/2, then solve cot²x − (√3 + 1) cot x + √3 = 0.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.110 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 176. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: Trigonometric Equations is an SAQ-ONLY unit, so the section is fixed by the unit rather than inferred. Printed appearances: AP 19. A quadratic in cot x, and the given range means NO general solution is wanted — only the values inside (0, π/2). ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Split the middle term
steps.margin_note: First mark. The middle coefficient is −(√3 + 1), which splits as −√3 and −1 — and their product √3 matches the constant.

recall.must_convey: That the middle term splits as −√3 cot x − cot x.
accept: split the middle term into minus root three cot x and minus cot x
the two parts multiply to give the constant root three
break the middle coefficient into root three and one
middle term ni root three and one ga split cheyyali
split the middle term

steps.why: The coefficient is already written as (√3 + 1), which names the two parts. The question hands over the split rather than hiding it.
common_mistakes: Using the quadratic formula on a surd coefficient.

steps.label: Factorise
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Group in pairs and take out the common factor from each — both give (cot x − √3).

accept: group in pairs and factor to get cot x minus one into cot x minus root three equals zero
both pairs share cot x minus root three
the factors are cot x minus one and cot x minus root three
pairs ga group chesi factor cheste rendu brackets vasthai
factorise the quadratic

steps.why: Both groups must leave the SAME bracket — if they do not, the split in step 1 was the wrong pair.
common_mistakes: Cancelling cot x from both sides.

steps.label: Convert to tan
steps.margin_note: Third mark. cot x = 1 gives tan x = 1, and cot x = √3 gives tan x = 1/√3 — turn them over, because the standard angles are named in tan.

recall.must_convey: That cot x = 1 and cot x = √3 give tan x = 1 and tan x = 1/√3.
accept: cot x equals one gives tan x equals one and cot x equals root three gives tan x equals one over root three
take the reciprocal of each value
convert both to tangent
cot ni tan ga marchali, reciprocal teeskovali
turn the cotangents into tangents

steps.why: cot and tan are reciprocals, so cot x = √3 means tan x = 1/√3 — not tan x = √3. That inversion is where marks are most often lost.
common_mistakes: Writing tan x = √3 from cot x = √3.
Leaving the answer in cot form.

steps.label: Pick the values in range
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The question fixes 0 < x < π/2, so give the two angles in that range only — no general solution.

recall.must_convey: That within 0 < x < π/2 the solutions are x = π/4 and x = π/6.
accept: in the given range the solutions are pi by four and pi by six
tan of pi by four is one and tan of pi by six is one over root three
no general solution is needed because the range is given
range lo pi by four and pi by six matrame
give only the values in the given range

steps.why: A stated range replaces the general solution. Writing nπ + π/4 here would include angles outside (0, π/2) and answer a different question.
common_mistakes: Writing the general solution nπ + α.
Giving only one of the two values.
